back_translation: I took all this to heart and examined it: the righteous and the wise, together with their works, are all in the hand of God. Man does not know whether love or hatred awaits him ahead.

Everything happens alike to everyone: the same event happens to the righteous and the wicked, to the good, to the clean and the unclean, to the one who offers sacrifice and the one who does not. As with the good man, so with the sinner; as with the one who swears an oath, so with the one who fears to swear.

This is an evil in everything done under the sun: the same event happens to all. Moreover, the hearts of the sons of men are full of evil, and madness is in their hearts throughout their lives — and after that they go to join the dead.
But whoever is still among all the living has hope, for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing at all. They have no further reward, for the remembrance of them is already forgotten.
Their love, their hatred, and their envy have long since perished. They no longer have any portion forever in all that is done under the sun.
Go, eat your food with joy, and drink your wine with a glad heart, for God has already favored your works.
Let your garments be clean white at all times, and do not let your head lack oil.

Enjoy life with the wife you love, all the days of your life without substance that He has given you under the sun — all your days without substance. For that is your portion in life and in the toil at which you toil under the sun.
Whatever your hand takes hold of to do, do it with all your strength, for in the realm of the dead, where you are going, there is no work, no reckoning, no knowledge, and no wisdom.

I saw something else under the sun: the race does not belong to the swift, nor the battle to the mighty, nor food to the wise, nor riches to the clever, nor favor to the skilled; for time and unexpected happenings befall them all.
For man does not know his time. Like fish caught in a cruel net and like birds caught in a snare, so the sons of men are trapped in an evil time when it falls upon them suddenly.
I have also seen this example of wisdom under the sun, and it was great in my eyes:
There was a small city with few people in it, and a great king came against it, besieged it, and built great siegeworks against it.
And in that city was found a poor wise man, and he saved the city by his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.
So I said, wisdom is better than strength; but the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not listened to.
The calm words of the wise are more worth hearing than the shouting of a ruler among fools.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but a single sinner destroys much good.
